statement: A contest has 24 questions. With one minute left, Max has answered 19 and cannot solve the rest. Wrong answers and blanks both score 0. How many more should he guess?

choices.misconception: I thought a blank was safer than a guess, so he should not guess at all.
I counted 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 and got 6, but question 19 is already answered.
I gave the number of questions he has already answered.
I gave the number of questions in the whole contest.

hints: Can a guess ever lose him points?
A wrong answer scores the same as a blank, so every guess can only add points. Max should guess on every question he has not answered. Count how many those are.
He has answered 19 of the 24 questions. Count on from 19 to 24 by the jumps, not the numbers.

solutions.reliable: A wrong guess scores 0, exactly like a blank, and a right guess scores points. So Max should guess on every question he has not answered. He has answered 19 of 24, so $24 - 19 = 5$ are left. He should guess on all 5. The idea to keep: when wrong answers cost nothing, fill in every blank before time runs out.

whyOnTest: Using the last minute to fill every blank is free points, and the trap answers come from fearing a guess or miscounting what is left.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
